# Embassy v1.7.1 — the broker stops lying to itself

One evening of routine restarts exposed four stacked reliability defects, and this release removes the class rather than the symptoms.

The big one: provider I/O ran under the same lane that serves status reads, callbacks, and observations — so one slow provider turn (a real 84-second first dispatch) froze the broker's self-knowledge for its whole duration, and the connector kept reporting "healthy" on frozen evidence afterward. Dispatch now prepares and performs entirely outside the commit lane with revalidation at the commit point; interruptions settle honestly and never replay; health degrades truthfully after 35 seconds without positive evidence, and observation age is visible everywhere.

Claude routes stop going stale across broker restarts: the selected session is re-observed at boot and on a fixed timer by exact UUID — including across the session's own restarts — through observation-only connections that structurally cannot send, pair, answer approvals, or touch credentials or history.

And when the Codex Desktop app is the problem, Embassy now says so: `embassy doctor` detects an orphaned Desktop and the private-App-Server split-brain (the failure that cost this project an evening of manual troubleshooting), names the condition on the dashboard in both languages, and prints the exact remedy. The v1.6 reconnect guidance, silently regressed in v1.7.0, renders again — now with a test built from the live incident snapshot.

Verification: 759 tests and the deliverability soak, green from an isolated worktree; five additional settlement corrections from adversarial review, each with its own regression test; a synthetic 90-second provider turn proving control, observations, and unrelated dispatch all continue.

Upgrade: `npm install -g agent-embassy@1.7.1`, restart your broker.
